neurons from isolated ganglion of Aplysii californica undergo dynamic volume changes in response to osmotic and sodium pump inhibition manipulations, and that these changes are reversible.

neuronal volume changes of greater than thirty percent can be observed when neurons from isolated Aplysia ganglia are subjected to long term blockade of sodium transport or to hypotonic or hypertonic solutions.
neurons in culture change their volume in response to alterations in the osmolarity of their bathing solution or when active sodium transport is blocked.

the role of volume in regulating neuronal function.
the effects of changes in the external environment of Aplysian neurons on neuronal volume.
the role of volume regulation in neuronal excitability and the possible relationship between volume changes and neurotransmitter release.

neuronal volume is not static and that it is a variable which may be manipulated by physiological manipulations.
the volume of neurons in the CNS of Aplysisa can increase or decrease by as much as 30% and that this change is reversible.
the volume of neurons is not static but is dynamic and can be altered in response to osmotic and ionic manipulations.

the neuronal volume may change dynamically and reversibly, depending on the external conditions, and that these changes may affect the neuronal functions.
neuronal volume changes may be important in the modulation of neuronal function.

the cell volume of neurons can change significantly and that this change can occur in response to changes in the osmolarity of solutions and to inhibition of active sodium transport.
